item.title: The PM Who Can Build
item.description:
I’m not a product manager, but watching PMs lean into AI has made me think they are in a particularly interesting position.

Good PMs spend their time understanding problems, setting priorities, and making trade-offs. They decide what belongs in the first version and what can wait. These are skills that take practice, and being able to write code does not automatically give you them.

A conversation between DHH and Lex Fridman helped bring this into focus for me. DHH argues that as AI takes on implementation, the ability to decide what software should do, and who it should serve, becomes central to building it.

item.title: The Return of the Bedroom Coder
item.description:
When I was a kid in the 80s, the idea of the bedroom coder felt almost magical.

You would read about someone building a game at home on a ZX Spectrum or a Commodore 64, and somehow that game could end up in the hands of players around the world. It made game development feel possible. Not easy, but possible.

It was one of the first examples I saw of software as a creative medium where one person with a computer and a good idea could make something real, ship it, and maybe even build a career from it.

item.title: Maker First, Leader Second
item.description:
There is a version of me on this blog that is still true, but no longer complete.

If you read through the older posts, you will find someone very close to the craft: building things, experimenting, writing about side projects, and occasionally disappearing down a rabbit hole about old computers or some tiny technical detail that felt too interesting to ignore. That person is still here.

But I am not only that person anymore.
